transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-05
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Ruiz (Redwood SA), Priya Rao (Lantern Head of Data), Tommy Li (Lantern Platform), Marcus Bee (Lantern DevOps), Elena Vázquez (Lantern GC)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery to map Lantern's residency constraints, KMS/key residency needs, and routing fallback rules. Aim is to determine fit for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and to scope a small benchmark focussed on EU residency and HIPAA-adjacent financial data.

Topics: KMS/key residency, region-specific routing, audit evidence (SOC2/HIPAA), log retention & redaction, private deployment feasibility, latency vs cost tradeoffs, next steps for benchmark.

Transcript (timestamps are approximate, auto-generated captions with occasional errors):
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, to kick off, quick intros, and then we want to really understand your constraints on data residency and keys.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya here. Quick context: Lantern is a regional savings bank in the EU with US customer segments. We're exploring LLM assist for customer service summaries and fraud scoring; legal's flagged residency and key ownership as blockers.
[00:25] Tommy Li: Yep, Tom from platform. We run most infra in eu-west-1, and latency budget for customer-facing features needs to be under 200 ms for the initial prompt ideally, sub-second overall.
[00:35] Alex Kim: Got it. Maya, Jordan - do you want to walk through hosting options briefly?
[00:39] Maya Patel: Sure. Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem). Hosted is fastest to get started but doesn't guarantee customer-managed KMS or key residency unless you use our Private offering. That said, we do provide region locking and strict subprocessors lists; apologies if some of our product names come out weird in transcript - like "reed wood" sometimes.
[01:05] Priya Rao: That's fine - tell us what guarantees we can get for keys and logs.
[01:09] Jordan Ruiz: For Private you can bring your own KMS or integrate with a Cloud HSM; keys can be kept in your tenant's control and we can also support an HSM-backed key in your VPC. For Dedicated, we offer customer-dedicated capacity with KMS options but with limited key residency guarantees depending on contract language.
[01:28] Elena Vázquez: Important: Lantern cannot have customer data leave the EU region for certain products. Also, audit trails need to be provable for regulatory exam with immutable logs for 7 years, and we need a clear subprocessor list.
[01:42] Alex Kim: Understood. Two separate things: (1) where inference executes and (2) where keys and logs live. We can pin execution to EU regions; for Hosted it depends on model availability in-region. For Private, everything stays in your VPC.
[01:58] Marcus Bee: Quick question: if we use Redwood Hosted but region-lock to eu-west-1, does any model agent or fallback ever go outside? We want explicit deconfliction for fallbacks.
[02:09] Maya Patel: By default routing policy prefers same-region endpoints; fallback to other regions only happens if you opt into multi-region failover. We can set policy to "no cross-border fallback" in the config - but that does reduce high-availability options.
[02:26] Tommy Li: And what about model variants or cached KV stores? Are those replicated cross-region?
[02:32] Jordan Ruiz: KV cache can be region-scoped. If you set per-tenant caching to EU-only, runtime won't sync to other regions. We have had impaired transcriptions before, sorry, so saying "KV" as "kay-vee" - but yes.
[02:44] Priya Rao: Okay. Next big thing is log content. We need to avoid storing full customer PII in logs. Does Redwood provide log redaction or sampling?
[02:54] Maya Patel: We provide configurable log redaction and token-level redaction options; we also offer minimal logging where only metadata and anonymized traces are kept. There may be limits to debugging if you redact everything.
[03:08] Priya Rao: Right, so for audit we need request IDs, timestamps, model version and a hash, but not the raw PII. Is that doable?
[03:16] Jordan Ruiz: Yes, typical pattern: produce deterministically salted hashes for identifiers in logs, store model metadata, response latencies, and then keep the actual prompts/outputs only in encrypted buckets if you choose.
[03:28] Elena Vázquez: We also need an SLA that the logs can be produced within 48 hours for regulatory requests.
[03:34] Alex Kim: SLA on evidence production - yes, we can commit to documented runbooks. For Hosted customers the process is more standardized; for Dedicated/Private we can support direct access to audit-ready logs in your retention store.
[03:47] Priya Rao: KMS: we want customer-managed keys, key residency in EU, and no automatic key escrow outside the EU, unless we sign a very specific legal framework.
[03:58] Maya Patel: Understood. Private option supports BYOK with an HSM in your cloud account. Dedicated can be configured to use your KMS via IAM roles; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default, but we can discuss bringing customer keys into a dedicated contract.
[04:14] Tommy Li: Any precedent with banks like us?
[04:16] Alex Kim: Yes - we've onboarded several financial customers on Dedicated and Private. We have a checklist and evidence pack (SOC2, HIPAA attestation, penetration test summary). I'll share that after this call.
[04:27] Marcus Bee: For dedicated capacity, what's the network topology? Do we get VPC peering or private link?
[04:33] Jordan Ruiz: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering depending on cloud provider; for Private installs we deploy into your VPC with private endpoints only.
[04:42] Priya Rao: Data residency also intersects with training/finetuning policies - we will not permit any training/weights updates using customer PII. Is Redwood's runtime ever used for fine-tuning customer data?
[04:54] Maya Patel: Our inference runtime does not automatically feed customer data back into training unless you explicitly enable data capture for model updates. We also allow you to opt-out of any telemetry used for model improvement.
[05:06] Elena Vázquez: On subpoenas and lawful access: we need a clear policy about subprocessors and country-level legal exposure.
[05:12] Alex Kim: We'll provide subprocessors list and contractual language. For Private deployments, subprocessors are effectively you and Redwood's support engineers if you allow them.
[05:23] Tommy Li: Switching gears: latency vs cost. If we pin to EU-only Dedicated GPUs, cost goes up. How does Redwood recommend balancing batch size and latency for a customer-facing microservice?
[05:35] Maya Patel: We usually start with low-concurrency, small-batch serving (batch size 1-2) to hit latency SLOs, then introduce smart batching and prefix KV caching for historical context to reduce tokens generated. For Dedicated we can tune kernels and quantization to reduce cost while keeping latency targets.
[05:51] Priya Rao: Can you run a short benchmark that simulates our workload? We have short prompts and occasional larger contexts for dispute reviews.
[05:58] Alex Kim: Absolutely. Proposed: 1) demo benchmark in eu-west-1 with 2 model sizes, 2) synthetic dataset with masked PII, 3) measure 95th latency and token cost. Maya will prepare.
[06:11] Priya Rao: How about HIPAA? We aren't healthcare but some of our data requires similar controls. We need to see HIPAA controls in the evidence pack.
[06:19] Alex Kim: We'll include HIPAA mappings where applicable.
[06:22] Elena Vázquez: I also need to understand retention and the right to delete. If a user requests deletion under GDPR, can we purge logs and training records?
[06:31] Jordan Ruiz: Yes - purge can be supported. For Hosted, deletion requests remove user data from active stores and mark backups for lifecycle deletion. For Private, you control retention. We'll need to map exact data flows to be definitive.
[06:46] Marcus Bee: One detail: key rotation. If Lantern rotates keys in KMS, does Redwood need a window to re-encrypt caches, or do you route to new key seamlessly?
[06:56] Maya Patel: With BYOK we integrate with your KMS rotation APIs; there is typically a short window where ephemeral caches are re-encrypted. We can coordinate rotation windows with your ops team to avoid service disruption.
[07:09] Priya Rao: What about test/dev environments? We can't use production PII in staging; is there a supported sandbox with masked data?
[07:16] Alex Kim: Yes - we recommend a sandbox in eu-west-1 with synthetic or masked data. We also offer a redacted logging profile for staging environments that keeps only metadata.
[07:26] Tommy Li: Any penalty for geo-fencing HA? If we turn off cross-region fallback, are we on the hook for downtime?
[07:33] Jordan Ruiz: If you disable cross-region failover, you accept regional availability limits. Dedicated contracts can include higher SLA or multi-az capacity within the same region to mitigate this.
[07:45] Priya Rao: For audit evidence, we need a clear chain: request ID -> model version -> config -> KMS key id -> retention tag. Can Redwood produce that out of the box?
[07:55] Maya Patel: Yes, we can emit that metadata per request. The only caveat is if you ask us to redact the prompt content fully, you'll still get the hash and metadata.
[08:06] Elena Vázquez: I'd like an example evidence export format. CSV or JSON with signed timestamps would be ideal.
[08:12] Alex Kim: We'll attach an export sample in the follow-up docs.
[08:16] Priya Rao: What about emergency legal holds? We sometimes need to freeze records for litigation hold.
[08:22] Jordan Ruiz: We support legal-hold tagging. When applied, retention is extended and deletion disabled until release. For Private, you manage these tags directly.
[08:33] Marcus Bee: Are there any known perf regressions with encryption-at-rest on Dedicated vs Hosted? We've seen 5-10% CPU overhead in other stacks.
[08:42] Maya Patel: Encryption overhead is minimal on modern GPUs; the biggest overhead is network encryption and additional I/O for audit logging if you're storing raw prompts. We can quantify this in the benchmark.
[08:54] Alex Kim: Let's open the floor for any constraints we missed.
[08:58] Priya Rao: One more: we need to ensure our legal team signs off on subprocessors in countries with surveillance laws.
[09:05] Elena Vázquez: Exactly - also want explicit commit that we won't be part of training corpora.
[09:09] Maya Patel: We'll include a non-training clause in the contract for Lantern scope.
[09:13] Tommy Li: And can we get an architecture diagram showing where logs, keys, and inference live?
[09:18] Alex Kim: We'll provide that in the follow-up pack.
[09:21] Priya Rao: Great. On timing - we need a pilot by end of Q2.
[09:25] Alex Kim: That's reasonable. We'll propose a 6-week pilot scope in the benchmark plan.
[09:29] Jordan Ruiz: For the pilot, suggested workstreams: security evidence review, sandbox benchmark, legal contract review, and ops runbook for key rotation and retention.
[09:39] Priya Rao: Sounds good.
[09:41] Elena Vázquez: Quick question - is there a separate support path for regulatory incidents?
[09:45] Maya Patel: Yes, enterprise support with 24/7 escalation and named reliability engineers is available on Dedicated/Private tiers.
[09:53] Marcus Bee: Ok, I want to flag we may need a short performance deep-dive with your SEs during the benchmark.
[09:58] Maya Patel: Happy to do that.
[10:00] Alex Kim: Great. Recap of next steps: Alex shares evidence pack and subprocessors list; Maya sends benchmark plan; schedule follow-up ops + legal deep dive week of 2027-03-15. Any other blockers?
[10:14] Priya Rao: No blockers from me. Thank you.
[10:17] Elena Vázquez: We'll gather legal Qs and return them before the follow-up.
[10:20] Tommy Li: I'll coordinate sample dataset creation and masking.
[10:23] Alex Kim: Thank you everyone. We'll follow up by email with the documents and calendar invites.
[10:28] (meeting ends)
